text:
jess: heads-up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes since yesterday evening (~19:00 UTC). tickets #4321/#4327. single-token streaming tails up to 6-10s intermittently. p95 up ~30%, p99 ~2x. stack: hosted API -> runtime shard pool. suspect KV/prefix cache thrash. anyone on?
rachael: looking now. dashboards show a big jump in prefix_kv_miss_rate starting 2026-02-27 18:55 UTC. p99 latency correlates with miss bursts on shards 7/8. grabbing prometheus queries and logs.
rachael: prometheus queries I'm using:
```
# 5m avg miss rate per shard
sum by (shard)(rate(kv_prefix_cache_misses_total[5m])) / sum by (shard)(rate(kv_prefix_cache_requests_total[5m]))

# eviction spikes
rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])
```
rachael: numbers: shard=7 miss_rate jumped 0.03 -> 0.38 between 18:55 and 19:20 UTC. evictions went from ~2/min to ~180/min. logs show repeated eviction loops:
```
2026-02-27T19:02:11Z shard=7 cache:evict key="pfx:usr:xyz:..." reason=mem_pressure
2026-02-27T19:02:11Z shard=7 cache:insert key="pfx:usr:abc:..." size=12
2026-02-27T19:02:11Z shard=7 cache:evict key="pfx:usr:abc:..." reason=mem_pressure
```
omar: I think I know the root cause. We rolled out model variant v2-quant yesterday (canary at 20%) and also shipped the header-normalization change in the same PR. header-normalization accidentally added raw user-scoped header `x-client-meta` into the cache key string for prefix caching. that made high cardinality keys -> thrash. repro in staging.
kai: confirmed local repro. steps:
1) run short bench with prefix warmup disabled: `go run ./bench -qps 50 -model v2-quant -warmup=false`
2) send requests with varying `x-client-meta` values (random trace ids)
3) watch `kv_prefix_cache_miss_rate` and p99 go up

kai: sample request that reproduces:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-client-meta: trace-$(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","prefix":"customer:123"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
omar: ok immediate mitigation options:
- roll back header-normalization change (hotfix). low risk and will reduce key cardinality immediately.
- increase prefix cache capacity for hot shards (FF/override) to buy time.
- add short TTL (2m) on prefix entries to avoid hot churn while we fix.
- route heavy customers to fallback model variant without the bug.

rachael: agree. i'm preparing a diag runbook for support. proposed short-term plan:
1) deploy hotfix to remove `x-client-meta` from cache key (PR opened)
2) bump cache_limit for shards 7/8 by 2x via feature-flag (FF name: ff.prefix_cache_capacity_shard_override)
3) add Prom alert: when global prefix_miss_rate > 0.2 for >5m -> page eng-runtime
4) start background warmup job to pre-populate prefixes for recent model variants

omar: PR #9876 opened to revert the header inclusion. canarying at 5% now. I'll monitor miss rate and memory usage. if canary green, ramp to 50% then 100%.
deploy-bot: deploy job started: canary rollout PR#9876 -> service/runtime (canary=5%).
rachael: support update posted to tickets. letting customers know we're on it and tracking regressions. added workaround: include `x-client-meta: normalized` as a temporary UX patch for clients that can opt-in.
jess: thanks. i've sent a short note to customer contacts and queued a follow-up for 2 hours with telemetry.
omar: quick note: we also discovered a separate cache key bug for rerank requests — the key used the entire request body instead of prefix+hash. added truncation + normalized whitespace in PR #9881 (nonblocking for the immediate incident but will reduce future variance).
kai: for long-term: propose switching eviction policy to LFU for prefix cache (LRU thrashes when high-cardinality bursts). also want to add adaptive warmup: when a new model variant is observed, run a small sample of warmup prefixes on cold shards.
rachael: adding action items to the incident doc:
- [ ] merge & fully roll PR#9876 (omar)
- [ ] FF bump shard capacity (rachael/ops)
- [ ] add TTL to prefix entries (dev-runtime)
- [ ] add Prom alert & dashboard panels (sre)
- [ ] schedule LFU eval & warmup job (kai)
- [ ] follow up with customers in 4h (jess)

omar: current status: canary at 25%, miss_rate on shard7 down from 0.38 -> 0.06 in canary subset, p99 tails reduced to ~1.1s in canary traffic. rolling to 100% over next 20m unless telemetry breaks.
deploy-bot: canary ramp to 100% completed for PR#9876.
rachael: verified metrics: global prefix_miss_rate back to baseline 0.04. p95/p99 trending back down. closing the immediate incident. will keep an eye for next 24h and follow up on long-term items.
jess: marked tickets as 'fix deployed' and scheduled retrospective with customers. thanks team :thumbsup:
